title: Antebrachial Fascia Release During Endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release
official: Antebrachial Fascia Proximal to Incision Release in Endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release
summary:
Carpal tunnel syndrome is a common condition caused by compression of the median nerve at the wrist. Endoscopic carpal tunnel release (ECTR) is a commonly performed surgical procedure used to relieve this compression. During ECTR, some surgeons also release the antebrachial fascia, while others do not. It is currently unclear whether release of the antebrachial fascia provides additional benefit when performed during routine ECTR.

The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to compare clinical and functional outcomes following ECTR with release of the antebrachial fascia versus ECTR without release of the antebrachial fascia. Participants undergoing ECTR will be randomly assigned to one of the two surgical approaches and followed for approximately 6 weeks after surgery. Study outcomes will include patient-reported outcome measures, clinical assessments, and complications to determine whether antebrachial fascia release affects recovery and postoperative outcomes.

interventions.name: Antebrachial Fascia Release During Endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release
Endoscopic Carpal Tunnel Release Without Antebrachial Fascia Release

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Able and willing to provide informed consent
* Available for study participation and follow-up
* Undergoing isolated unilateral or bilateral endoscopic carpal tunnel release (ECTR) for carpal tunnel syndrome

Exclusion Criteria:

* Age younger than 18 years
* Incarcerated individuals
* Unwilling or unable to provide informed consent or participate in study procedures
* Additional upper extremity injuries
* Concurrent upper extremity surgical procedures on the same side as the ECTR
* Other related upper extremity injuries on the same side as the ECTR
* Undergoing revision carpal tunnel release
